A1.justification: Both complete 41-page PDFs describe the same F-EDL research. The main text, checklist, and Appendices A–G align, with readable text, equations, tables, and figures supporting reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original F-EDL classification and uncertainty-estimation experiments, ablations, timing measurements, and qualitative analyses in Section 6 and Appendices E–G.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including benchmark comparisons, parameter and regularization ablations, and uncertainty visualizations.

M1.justification: The FD parameter heads, spectral normalization, expected-MSE plus Brier regularization objective, and prediction and uncertainty procedures are unchanged in Section 3 and Algorithms 1–2.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same CIFAR-10, CIFAR-100, CIFAR-10-LT, and DMNIST settings with the same OOD and corruption datasets. New citations concerning semiconductor applications and imbalanced learning do not introduce experiments in those domains.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged within corresponding experiments, including the EDL variants, Dropout, task-specific MSP/DDU comparisons, and PostNet/DUQ in Appendix F's Table 11. Newly cited methods are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Section 6.1 and Appendix E retain the same data splits, imbalance ratios, corruption severities, architectures, training budgets, and evaluation metrics. The training-size and qualitative-analysis protocols also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The parameter-fixing and regularization ablations in Tables 5, 15, and 16, corruption evaluation, training-size analysis in Figure 4, and ambiguous-input analyses in Appendix G are unchanged.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across five random trials in checklist item 7. Table 9 retains its five-run timing summary, and no uncertainty-reporting or statistical procedure changes.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, F-EDL's CIFAR-10 accuracy remains 91.19 ± 0.2 in Table 1, and DMNIST-to-FMNIST OOD AUPR remains 99.76 ± 0.1 in Table 4.

T1.justification: Section 4's formal statements and the derivations and proofs in Appendices A and C, including Theorem C.1, are unchanged. Citation renumbering does not alter the mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims about flexible Dirichlet modeling, efficient uncertainty estimation, theoretical properties, and strong performance across classical, long-tailed, and noisy settings.

C2.justification: Mechanism explanations and result interpretations remain unchanged. Section 7 retains the limitations concerning classification-only applicability, incomplete uncertainty disentanglement, and dependence on external regularization; added citations do not revise these arguments.

D1.justification: The code-access statement, algorithms, preprocessing descriptions, hyperparameters, MLP specifications, and GPU disclosures are unchanged in Section 6 and Appendix E. No new reproducibility information is supplied.

R1.justification: v2 adds nine references, increasing the bibliography from 59 to 68 while retaining every earlier work. Citations added in Sections 1, 5, 7, and G.2 cover OOD detection, semiconductor applications, imbalanced learning, logit adjustment, and contextual anomalies, without substantially revising research positioning.

P1.justification: Citation insertions, reference renumbering, and the arXiv version/date text change. The substantive prose, terminology, section order, and appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Added references reflow the bibliography on pages 11–14, and citation changes cause limited local text reflow. All six figures and sixteen tables retain their content, design, and placement, apart from citation-number updates in some captions.

improvement.justification: v2 supplies additional literature pointers in existing passages, with minor accompanying layout changes. The scientific arguments, theoretical and empirical evidence, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged, so the bibliographic expansion produces no meaningful overall quality difference.
